Huang, Yang and Aitkin (2016) DBH–height models for Alberta tree species

Source: R/hd_huang2016.R
hd_huang2016.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the population-level individual-tree height–diameter models in Huang, Yang and Aitkin (2016; Alberta Tech. Rep. T/609). Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm), optionally by natural-subregion group.

Usage

hd_huang2016(DBH, species, natural_subregion = NULL, keep_model_id = FALSE)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m above ground), in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "PICE.GLA"; compact "PICEGLA" is accepted), or one of "DECID", "CONIF", "ALL" for the source's combined models.

natural_subregion

Optional. Plot level. Alberta natural subregion (Natural Regions Committee 2006), given either as the numeric code 1–21 or the character code (e.g. "CM" = Central Mixedwood, "LF" = Lower Foothills, "UF" = Upper Foothills), as listed in Table 2 of the source. Length 1 or length(DBH). NULL (default) uses the provincial models.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add columns model_id ("huang2016") and subregion_group (the natural-subregion group of the model used, e.g. "7-9", or "provincial").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id and subregion_group.

Details

Model scope (species coverage): aspen (POPU.TRE), balsam poplar (POPU.BAL), white birch (BETU.PAP), lodgepole pine (PINU.CON), white spruce (PICE.GLA), black spruce (PICE.MAR), balsam fir (ABIE.BAL), Douglas-fir (PSEU.MEN), tamarack (LARI.LAR) and jack pine (PINU.BAN). Following the source species grouping (Table 1), whitebark pine (PINU.ALB) and limber pine (PINU.FLE) use the lodgepole pine equations, Engelmann spruce (PICE.ENG) uses white spruce, subalpine fir (ABIE.LAS) uses balsam fir, and western (LARI.OCC) and alpine larch (LARI.LYA) use tamarack; a one-time message reports the mapping. The source's combined models are selected with species = "DECID" (all deciduous species), "CONIF" (all conifers) or "ALL" (all species combined).

Model forms: deciduous species and "DECID" use eq. [1], $$H = 1.3 + b_1 [1 - \exp(-b_2 DBH)]^{b_3};$$ conifers, "CONIF" and "ALL" use eq. [2], $$H = 1.3 + b_1 / (1 + \exp[b_2 + b_3 \ln(DBH + 0.01)]).$$

Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured at 1.3 m, so predicted height tends to 1.3 m as DBH tends to 0.

Population-level prediction: coefficients are those of the base (fixed-effects) models in Table 4, which the source recommends for trees in plots without height measurements (Section 6). Plot-specific calibration with the mixed models (Table 5) is not implemented.

Variants (natural-subregion groups): if natural_subregion is NULL (default) the provincial models are used. Otherwise the model for the species' natural-subregion group is used (e.g. white spruce: subregions 7–9, 10, 11, and 1–6 and 12–21). Species fitted only at the provincial level (BETU.PAP, PSEU.MEN, LARI.LAR, PINU.BAN and their mapped species, and the combined models), and rows with NA natural_subregion, use the provincial model. One-time messages report which variant is used.

Rows with NA DBH or species return NA height. DBH values outside the range of the fitting data of the selected model (Table 3) are computed and reported in a single warning.

References

Huang, S., Yang, Y., and Aitkin, D. (2016). Updated population and plot-specific individual tree height-diameter models for major Alberta tree species. Report #4, Tech. Rep. Pub. No. T/609. Forestry Division, Alberta Agriculture and Forestry, Edmonton, Alberta.

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

# Provincial models
hd_huang2016(DBH = c(10, 25, 40), species = c("PICE.GLA", "POPU.TRE", "PINU.CON"))
#> hd_huang2016(): `natural_subregion` not supplied; using the provincial models.
#> This message is displayed once per session.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   9.94
#> 2  22.7 
#> 3  26.7 

# Natural-subregion-group models (Lower Foothills), numeric or character code
hd_huang2016(DBH = 25, species = "PICE.MAR", natural_subregion = "LF")
#> hd_huang2016(): using natural-subregion-group models where available.
#> This message is displayed once per session.
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   19.5
hd_huang2016(DBH = 25, species = "PICE.MAR", natural_subregion = 11,
             keep_model_id = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   height model_id  subregion_group
#>    <dbl> <chr>     <chr>          
#> 1   19.5 huang2016 11             

# Combined conifer model
hd_huang2016(DBH = 30, species = "CONIF")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   24.1
